docs.title: citydb-3dtiler
docs.text:
A 3DTiles sample represents the city objects of Leipzig city

This application is in the testing phase

This application is still in the testing phase. Please exercise caution when using it in production. Therefore, feedback is always welcome. Please feel free to create an issue on the GitHub page or contact me: murat.kendir(At)tum.de

citydb-3dtiler can generate 3DTiles (v 1.0 and 1.1) by reading features (formerly known as "cityobject"s) from 3DCityDB (v5.x), a database application that can import CityGML 2.0 or 3.0-based datasets. The application's key features are as follows:

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• creates singular or separate 3DTiles (based on object classes) by reading the features from the 3DCityDBv5.
  • generates report (advice.yml) about the existing data in the database and calculate the most efficient configuration parameters for creating 3D Tiles.
  • can assign simple colors or PBR materials based on object classes or the specified property values of features.
  • The PBR Materials of the 3D Tilesets can be customized with a CSV file by listing objectclasses and properties.
  • features can be filtered using SQL or CQL2 expressions
  • filters the features using different criterias such as id, limit, start-index, boundary box or type-name (object class)
  • filters the relevant attributes and can flatten the structure of complex attributes (such as con:Height)
  • supports 3DTiles v1.0 and v1.1
  • The Execution Times of the tiling mechanism depends on the given command, available dataset and the hardware. If you are curious about the execution times of some previously generated test visit this page.
This application requires database user credentials with read and write privileges.

Since the application generates 3DTiles based on the existing data in the database, additional views and tables may be created in the database. For this reason, users need read and write privileges on the database. A solution is planned for users who have read-only privileges.

docs.title: Special Thanks
docs.text:
This application is based on two important concepts and aims to bridge the gap between the concepts 3DTiles and CityGML. To bridge this gap, two main elements have been used in this software: 3DCityDB v5, pg2b3dm

We would like to take this opportunity to thank Bert Temme, the developer of the pg2b3dm library, and all 3DCityDB developers.

docs.title: Simple Usage (via Docker)
docs.text: There are two different ways to use citydb-3dtiler: using Docker containers and setting up a Python environment on the local computer to run the application. Both methods are explained in more detail on the relevant pages (How to use with Docker, How to use with Python Env). Below, Docker usage will be explained with only the fundamental steps.

docs.title: advise Command
docs.text: The advise command creates a report file in YAML format by examining the existing data in the database. This report file lists the main options used by the user in the command, the feature types in the database, the attributes of the features, and the recommended number of features per tile for conversion to the 3DTiles format. Unless otherwise specified by the user, this value is used during the tiling process.

docs.title: --help (-h)
docs.text:
If you use the help option after the advise command, you will see the usage syntax of that command which is like below.

advise [-h] [--ignore-thematic-surfaces] [-o [Output File Name]]

docs.title: --ignore-thematic-surfaces
docs.text:
This option used to ignore the thematic surfaces in the advice.yaml file. So, that means only the volumetric objects and some terrain related surfaces will be listed and reported. Others, like WindowSurface, RoofSurface etc., will be ignored. Default value is False.

  • Example : --ignore-thematic-surfaces

docs.title: --output-file (-o)
docs.text:
This option can be used if the user request to use a custom name for the advice file. Both of the file name and the file extension must be written.

  • Example : --output-file paris_2024.yml

docs.title: CLI Overview
docs.text:
citydb-3dtiler is the main command of the application. When run with the Docker container, this main command is automatically invoked, so there is no need to retype it. However, when running in a Python environment, the main command must be typed. Besides the main command, there are two subcommands: advise and tile. The --help option provides explanatory information about the typed command and, depending on the command, other options that can be used.

Where can i find installation instructions in more detail?

If you are planning to install citydb-3dtiler on a Python Virtual Environment and are looking for a more detailed instruction, visit this page: How to use with Python Virtual Environment?. Docker usage is briefly explained here and also described in more detail on the citydb-3dtiler Docker page.

The usage syntax of the main options and the subcommands advice and tile are as follows. To see this usage syntax on the command line interface (CLI), you can type -h or --help immediately after the main command (citydb-3dtiler) or the docker (run) command. What is the purpose of the backslash (\) character in the code block?
  • When typing commands, the caret (^), backtick (`), and backslash (\) are "escape characters" that tell the computer to handle the next symbol as plain text, not as a command.
  • Windows CMD uses ^, PowerShell uses `, and Linux Bash uses \ because each system speaks a slightly different language.
  • Alternatively, you can copy these commands into a text editor and delete both the escape characters and the new line characters (\n) to turn the command into a single line.

docs.title: Database Connection Options
docs.text:
This section lists the options that can be used to connect to the 3DCityDB (v5.x) database.

If you do not have a 3DCityDB (v5) instance...

If you do not have a 3DCityDB (v5) installation, visit the relevant section on the main documentation page.

docs.title: --db-host (-H)
docs.text:
-H or --db-host is used for specifying the computer name or the IP address of the database instance.

  • example: --db-host COMP01 or --db-host 192.168.2.3)

docs.title: --db-port (-P)
docs.text:
-P or --db-port is used to specify the port number that was defined during the database installation or forwarded by the 3DCityDB docker container

What if the forwarded port of the 3DCityDB does not work?

If you notice that the forwarded database port of the 3DCityDB (might be running as a Docker container) is not working in your environment, or let's say if you are not sure about the port number, try using the docker inspect [Container Name] command to expose the IP address and port of the running container. Then you can try changing the computer name or the IP address or even the port number with the exposed values (for example: --db-host 172.17.0.2 --db-port 5432). The same test can also be performed using other database clients such as pgAdmin.

docs.title: --db-name (-d)
docs.text: -d or --db-name is used to specify the database name.

docs.title: --db-schema (-S)
docs.text:
-S or --db-schema is used to specify the schema name of the 3DCityDB instance. If the schema name was not changed for a specific purpose during the installation, you do not need to use this option.

  • Default value is "citydb".

docs.title: --db-username (-u)
docs.text: -u or --db-username is used to specify the database username.

docs.title: --db-password (-p)
docs.text: -p or --db-password is used to specify the database password.

docs.title: Filter Options
docs.text: This section lists the options that can be used to filter objects with respect to different aspects.

docs.title: --limit
docs.text: It can be used to specify a limit number to reduce the selected features.

docs.title: --start-index
docs.text:
It can be used to specify the starting index (known as "Offset" in SQL context) of the selected features.

What kind of order is considered while using start-index?

The order considered when using --start-index is the existing order in the feature table in the database. This order may not match the order of features within the file you are importing.

docs.title: --id (-i)
docs.text:
ID number(s) (citydb.feature.objectid in the database) of specific feature(s).

Use comma as id number separator for multiple inputs and do not add space character between the id numbers.

  • Example : --id 9876,1234,8765,2345
What is the objectid?

objectid in the feature table were also known as gmlid in the former versions of the 3DCityDBs, which is the same value with the gml:id attributes in the imported CityGML or CityJSON file.

docs.title: --type-name (-t)
docs.text:
Type name of the features or a set of type names (aka ObjectClass).

Use comma as type name separator for multiple inputs and do not add space character between the type names

  • Example : --type-name WallSurface,RoofSurfaceSurface,GroundSurface

docs.title: --bbox (-b)
docs.text:
A bounding box element containing the x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max, and SRID values, to be used as the filtering geometry. Use comma as separator and do not add space character between the min/max values.

  • Example : --bbox 564822,5932935,566924,5934737,25832
What if the SRID value is not specified?

If the SRID value is not specified, than the current SRID (EPSG Code Number) in the database will be assumed as the common CRS.

SRID Values

If you are not sure about the CRS/SRS value of your dataset, you can search for the term srsName in the imported file or check the data in the database_srs table within the citydb schema in your database. The given SRID value must be a predefined CRS Code available in EPSG.io.

docs.title: --bbox-mode
docs.text:
This option can be used to specify the method of the boundary box usage as the filtering geometry. There are four options to select:

  • intersects (default value):
    • It uses spatial indexes, but not exact geometries, to query any intersection. (Fast, but less reliable results)
  • intersects-precise :
    • It uses both spatial indexes and geometries to query any intersection. (Slower, but more reliable results)
  • contains :
    • It uses spatial indexes, but not exact geometries, to query any containment case. (Fast, but less reliable results)
  • contains-precise :
    • It uses both spatial indexes and geometries to query any containment case. (Slower, but more reliable results)
must always be used with --bbox option

--bbox-mode option must always be used together with --bbox.

  • Example : --bbox 564822,5932935,566924,5934737,25832 --bbox-mode intersects-precise

docs.title: --filter (-f)
docs.text:
CQL2 filter expression.

Use the attribute names listed in the advice.yml file exactly as they are written in the file ( Common pattern : [NAMESPACE]_[PROPERTY] ). Use ~geom to refer to the geometry column.

  • Example : --filter "gen_revision_jahr >= 2021"
  • Example : s_overlaps(~geom,BBOX(9.978199, 53.541309, 10.010294, 53.557241, 4326)
Must be wrapped in quotes

Both SQL and CQL2 filters' arguments must be wrapped in quotes. An example: --filter "bldg_usage ='1100'". You can use the single quotes to use encapsulate the internal string values.

What if spatial operator fails against 3D geometries?

If the selected spatial operator does not work with the 3D geometries, try to use : 'st_envelope(~geom)' or st_convexhull(~geom) (would give more reliable results)

docs.title: --sql-filter
docs.text:
The SQL Filter accepts WHERE conditions just as they are written in standard SQL queries. Use '~geom' to refer to the geometry column.

  • Example : bldg_usage = ‘residential’ AND bldg_height__measured_height > 12.5

docs.title: Main Options
docs.text:
Check all the subcommands and the options in one diagram

If you want to see all the subcommands and the options with possible arguments in one diagram, visit this page : citydb-3dtiler Functionality Matrix

docs.title: --tiler-app
docs.text:
If the file name of the tiler application is different, you can use this option.

  • Default value is "pg2b3dm".
What is planned for this option?

We plan to enable the use of the i3dmExport and/or py3dtiles applications with this option in future developments. However, currently only the pg2b3dm application has been tested and is ready for use.

docs.title: --tilers-path
docs.text:
If you want to use a specific version of pg2b3dm that you have determined, you must put this specific version into another folder and then specify the folder path using this option. This way, you can make the application work with any version you want.

  • Default value is "tiler_app".
Some (tile) options might not work in this scenario

Since the options of the pg2b3dm application may vary depending on the version, you may not be able to use every argument.

docs.title: --ignore-thematic-surfaces
docs.text: This option used to ignore the thematic surfaces that descend from AbstractThematicSurface, such as WallSurface, WindowSurface etc.

docs.title: Difference between the Docker and Python Env. Usage
docs.text:
There are two main ways to use the citydb-3dtiler application: The first and relatively easier one is to run it inside a container using the Docker image. It does not require any installation other than Docker, but the parameters specified in the documentation must be used. The second way is to set up a Python virtual environment and run the application within that environment. It requires installation, but the commands are shorter. For this reason, we will list the Python commands in the example commands below. If you want to run the example commands below using a Docker container, all you need to do is simply replace the python3 citydb-3dtiler.py expression in the commands with the docker run ... expression.

Here below there are examples for such a replacement:

Take report within Python setupTake report using Docker 
python3 citydb-3dtiler.py \
--db-host localhost --db-port 9876 \
--db-name citydb-visualizer \
--db-schema citydb \
--db-username tester --db-password louvre \
advise

--rm --interactive --tty \
--name citydb-3dtiler \
--volume ./:/home/tester/citydb-3dtiler/shared:rw \
citydb-3dtiler:latest \
--db-host localhost --db-port 9876 \
--db-name citydb-visualizer --db-schema citydb \
--db-username tester --db-password louvre \
advise
What is the purpose of the backslash (\) character in the code block?
  • When typing commands, the caret (^), backtick (`), and backslash (\) are "escape characters" that tell the computer to handle the next symbol as plain text, not as a command.
  • Windows CMD uses ^, PowerShell uses `, and Linux Bash uses \ because each system speaks a slightly different language.
  • Alternatively, you can copy these commands into a text editor and delete both the escape characters and the new line characters (\n) to turn the command into a single line.

However, you still need to find the value sets for the existing dataset. After that you can add the property names and the values to the materials document like below:

namespace of classname classname namespace of property property name column name of property value property value pbr metallic roughness base color bldg Building #00E5EE80 bldg Building bldg roofType val_string flat #66DEF3FC bldg Building bldg roofType val_string gabled #F35FCBFC Style-Modes

Default style-mode is objectclass-based. Check the materials_for_features.csv table to view existing objectclasses.

    python3 citydb-3dtiler.py \

docs.title: style-absence-behaviour
docs.text:
citydb-3dtiler will try to assign material based on the features' properties and if not succeeded for a specific feature, it will try to assign an existing appearance (usually stored in the surface_data table).

docs.title: tile Command
docs.text: With the tile command, features in the database are converted to the 3DTiles format. The generated tilesets are saved under the shared folder in the directory where the program is executed. If the --separate-tilesets option is used, a separate folder is created within the shared folder for each tileset according to the separation argument (namespace or objectlass name), and the 3DTiles files are stored into these folders.

docs.title: --help (-h)
docs.text:
If you use the help option after the tile command, you will see the usage syntax of that command which is like below.

tile [-h] \
    [--style-mode {existing-appearances,property-based,objectclass-based,no-style}] \
    [--style-absence-behavior {fall-down,rise-up}] \
    [-o [Output Folder]] \
    [--transparency {blend,mask,opaque}] \
    [--custom-style [Name of the custom style file]] \
    [-a {none,selected,all}] \
    [--selected-attributes [Comma separated list of the selected attributes]] \
    [--attribute-structure {flat,nested}] \
    [--tiles-version {1.0,1.1}] \
    [--vertical-offset [VERTICAL_OFFSET]]

docs.title: --separate-tilesets
docs.text:
This option is used to specify the criteria for creating multiple tilesets. You can create separate tilesets by considering the objectclasses (Building, Wall, Window etc.) or namespaces (bldg, tun, brid etc.) of the features.

  • Example : --separate-tilesets objectclass

A Sample 3D Scene contains separate tilesets

docs.title: --style-mode
docs.text:
Style mode is used to assign material styles to features. Customizing PBR materials using the given CSV file is not the only option. There are four different style modes, and there is a mechanism (called style-absence-behaviour) that switches to another mode in case a style mode cannot be applied to a feature. The four style modes are like below:

  • existing-appearances :
    • When this option is selected, tiling application will try to derive the defined appearences in the database (not the textures yet, but only the materials).
  • property-based :
    • If you decided to assign colors to the features by considering some attributes, you can fill the relevant columns in materials_for_features.csv file and then select this option.
  • objectlass-based (default value) :
    • This mode is the default value for this option and it simply assigns the defined materials for every individual objectlass by considering the relevant columns in materials_for_features.csv file.

  • no-style :

    • In this option, there will be no different material for the features. Every feature will be rendered within the color specified in the materials_for_features.csv file in the column pbr_metallic_roughness_base_color for the pseudo-feature called anything-else.

  • Example : --style-mode existing-appearances

An example Scene for the property-based styling option

docs.title: --style-absence-behaviour
docs.text:
This option can be switched when a special absence behaviour is requested. The default behaviour is fall-down. This means that, for example, if the user selected the property-based style mode but the application could not find any value for the specified property, it will try to assign material according to the style mode at the next lower level; in this case, that mode will be objectclass-based. Only one of the following arguments expected :

  • fall-down (default value)
  • rise-up
What is the order of the style modes?

The vertical order of the style modes is exactly the same as their order in the help documents. The first mode is at the top, and the last mode is at the bottom. Therefore, the vertical order should be accepted from top to bottom as follows: existing-appearances, property-based, objectclass-based, no-style.

docs.title: --output-folder
docs.text: Generated tilesets are stored directly in the shared folder. However, you can specify a folder name in which the tilesets will be stored.

docs.title: --transparency
docs.text:
This is the option that determines the transparency of materials. Default value is opaque. Only one of the following arguments expected :

  • blend :
    • When set to this, the last two digits of the color codes in the CSV file (the RGBA code) will determine the amount of transparency.
  • mask :
    • When the masking option is selected, object textures are not rendered when they fall below a certain alpha value (this option has not been tested yet).

  • opaque (default value):

    • When set to opaque, any transparency value assigned to materials in the CSV file will be ignored even if present.

  • Example : --transparency-mode blend

docs.title: --custom-style
docs.text:
If you want to provide a custom style file (any CSV file not named materials_for_features), you can specify the file name (inc. file extension : .csv) using this argument.

  • Example : --custom-style materials_for_traffic_areas.csv

docs.title: --attributes (-a)
docs.text:
Available attributes can be ignored, filtered out, or selected as a whole. These attributes can be queried in the CesiumJS environment (they cannot be queried in QGIS for now) or used for interactive styling via additional JavaScript code. To specify which option fits your workflow, you can select one of the following options:

  • none (default value)
  • selected (use the --selected attributes option together)

  • all

  • Example : --attributes all

docs.title: --selected-attributes
docs.text:
Selected attributes must be listed with their exact names as they appear in the advice.yml file. The list separator is a comma, and no space characters should be used.

  • Example : --attributes selected --selected-attributes core_name,con_height,gen_citygrid_unitid
Where can i find the exact names of the attributes?

Check the advice.yml file to see the exact names of the available attributes.

docs.title: --attribute-structure
docs.text:
If you want to view the attributes as a flat/tabular data structure, select the “flat” option (default). If you want to view them as a nested structure, just as they are (in a JSON-like stucture), select the “nested” option.

  • flat (default value)
  • nested
Are the JSON-like nested attributes visible on CesiumJS?

Yes, they are visible on CesiumJS. However, if you want to display them in a foldable / unfoldable tree-like widget, you need to write additional JavaScript code. Otherwise, they would appear just like ordinary JSON text.

docs.title: --tiles-version
docs.text:
3D Tilesets can be generated in two versions : 1.0 and 1.1. If you are curious about the differences between these versions, we would highly recommend to visit the standard's OGC documentation page.

  • 1.0

  • 1.1

  • Example : --tiles-version 1.0

A video shows the usage of the 3DTiles v1.0 on QGIS Desktop

How can i show the 3DTiles on QGIS Desktop app?

There are multiple methods to visualize the 3DTiles on the QGIS Desktop (using CesiumIon plugin etc.). If you just want to visualize the 3DTiles on QGIS Desktop without using any cloud storage, then you need to generate the 3DTiles in the version 1.0. Store the tileset into your computer within version 1.0, then simply locate the tileset.json file in QGIS Desktop.

docs.title: --vertical-offset
docs.text:
Specify the vertical offset as a float number (for exp. 0.15 / -1.25) in meter unit. Do not use comma as decimal separator.

  • Example : --vertical-offset 0.15 | --vertical-offset -0.55

docs.title: --vertical-offset-from-csv
docs.text:
Assign the vertical offsets using the CSV file. Use the dot as the decimal separator.

Default vertical offsets for TrafficArea, AuxiliaryTrafficArea and Markings

There is a predefined +10 cm vertical offset for the TrafficArea and AuxiliaryTrafficArea objects, and a +15 cm vertical offset is also defined for the Marking objects. It is recommended to preserve these values so that the markings remain visible on top of the road objects, and the area objects on top of the other ground surfaces.

  • Example : --vertical-offset-from-csv

source env/bin/activate
